title: Production only changes via an explicit promote step
asA: operator responsible for what production serves
iWant: no code path that changes production as a side effect of a merge
soThat: every ship is a deliberate act with a named principal on the record

acceptanceCriteria.description: The project's CI workflow set contains no workflow that both triggers on `push` to main AND calls the Deploy Adapter's `promoteVersion` verb (or the vendor's coupled deploy verb `wrangler deploy`).
acceptanceCriteria.given: the CI workflow set of a project that has applied the blueprint
acceptanceCriteria.when: a lint scan walks every workflow file and inspects the trigger set of each and the deploy verb it invokes
acceptanceCriteria.then: no workflow file both matches trigger `push` on branch `main` (or a linear-history proxy) AND invokes a promote verb; the scan reports zero offenders

acceptanceCriteria.description: The `promote` workflow triggers only on explicit manual operator action, not on any push, pull-request, or schedule.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the only trigger present is the platform's explicit-manual-trigger primitive (`workflow_dispatch` on GitHub Actions or the equivalent) and no `push`, `pull_request`, or `schedule` trigger appears

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every successful promote leaves a structured record naming the version id promoted, the operator principal, the previously-serving version id, and the timestamp.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a successful invocation of the `promote` workflow
acceptanceCriteria.when: the deploy log store is inspected after the run
acceptanceCriteria.then: a new record exists whose fields include `promotedVersionId`, `promotedBy`, `previousVersionId`, and `promotedAt`; every field is populated and no field carries a secret value
